question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

Go back to your image description.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Definition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Description" means a spoken or written account that explains what somebody or something is like. (विवरण / वर्णन)

◦ "Definition" means a statement of the exact meaning or nature of something, and among the given options it is the closest in sense, since both words explain what a thing is.

◦ Example: The description (the definition) attached to the image tells you exactly what it shows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Deception" = the act of deliberately misleading somebody; trickery — almost the opposite of an honest account.

• Option 3 "Plan" = a detailed proposal for doing something in the future.

• Option 4 "Function" = the purpose or role of a person or thing.

NOTE

• Synonyms of description: account, portrayal, depiction, characterisation, definition, explanation.

• Word family: describe (verb), description (noun), descriptive (adjective) — note the change from -ibe to -ip in the noun form.

• Do not confuse deception (trickery) with description and discretion (the quality of behaving with judgement).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Disease that spreads over a whole country or the whole world
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pandemic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Pandemic" is a disease that spreads over a whole country or the whole world, affecting a very large number of people. (महामारी — विश्वव्यापी)

◦ The prefix "pan-" means all/whole, and "demos" means people — hence affecting all the people.

◦ Example: COVID-19 was declared a pandemic by the World Health Organization (WHO) in March 2020.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Rustic" = relating to the countryside; simple and rural.

• Option 3 "Panacea" = a remedy or cure for all diseases and problems (a cure-all) — a tempting trap because of the same prefix.

• Option 4 "Epidermis" = the outer layer of the skin.

NOTE

• Learn the ladder of disease spread: Sporadic (occurring occasionally) → Endemic (regularly found in a particular area) → Epidemic (spreading rapidly in a community at one time) → Pandemic (spreading across countries or the world).

• Other pan- words: panorama (an all-round view), pantheism, pan-Indian.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The radio data shows neither evidence for ongoing jet activity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. neither evidence for

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the use of "neither", which is wrong here for two reasons.

◦ "Neither" is used for two things and normally works in the pair "neither ... nor ...". Here there is only one thing (evidence) and no 'nor' anywhere in the sentence.

◦ The correct word to negate a single noun is "no": shows no evidence.

◦ Corrected sentence: The radio data shows no evidence for ongoing jet activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment "The radio data shows" is acceptable — "data" is commonly treated as a singular mass noun in modern usage, so "shows" is fine.

• Segment "ongoing jet activity." is correct — the adjective ongoing properly qualifies the uncountable noun activity.

NOTE

• Correlative pairs must always be completed: neither–nor, either–or, both–and, not only–but also, whether–or.

• Use neither for two items and none for more than two: Neither of the two came; None of the five came.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

If I was a clown, I would have made everyone smile.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. If I was a clown,

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is "was" in the if-clause. The sentence expresses an imaginary or unreal situation, so the subjunctive mood is required, which uses "were" for all subjects.

◦ Rule: in unreal conditions and after wish, as if, as though, if only, suppose, we use were — If I were you, He talks as if he were the boss.

◦ Corrected sentence: If I were a clown, I would have made everyone smile.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "I would have made" is acceptable as the result clause of the imaginary condition in this sentence.

• Segment "everyone smile." is correct — after the causative verb "make", the bare infinitive (without 'to') is used: make somebody smile/laugh/cry.

NOTE

• The three main conditionals: Type 1 (real) – If it rains, I will stay; Type 2 (unreal present) – If it rained, I would stay; Type 3 (unreal past) – If it had rained, I would have stayed.

• Causative structures: make/let + object + base verb; have + object + base verb; get + object + to-infinitive.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

According to the politician, using vulgar language to ______ votes is not something he will endorse.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. garner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Garner" means to gather, collect or acquire something, especially support, information or votes. (एकत्र करना / बटोरना)

◦ "Garner votes" is a standard political collocation, so it fits the blank perfectly.

◦ Correct: ... using vulgar language to garner votes is not something he will endorse.

◦ The verb is also used with praise, attention and support: The film garnered critical acclaim.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "segregate" = to separate or set apart from others — the opposite idea of gathering.

• Option 2 "divulge" = to reveal a secret or private information.

• Option 3 "lump" = to put together in a single group indiscriminately (to lump things together); it does not collocate with votes.

NOTE

• Synonyms of garner: gather, accumulate, amass, collect, procure, harvest.

• "Endorse" in the sentence means to approve or support publicly; it also means to sign the back of a cheque.

• A garner as a noun originally meant a granary or storehouse for grain, which explains the sense of gathering.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The teacher had reading the instructions aloud to the students.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. had read the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The auxiliary "had" forms the past perfect tense, which requires the past participle (V3) of the main verb — not the -ing form.

◦ Verb forms: read (V1) – read (V2) – read (V3) — spelt the same but pronounced reed – red – red.

◦ So "had reading" must become "had read".

◦ Corrected sentence: The teacher had read the instructions aloud to the students.

◦ The sentence is active, since the teacher performs the action, so no passive form is needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had been read the" is passive and would wrongly suggest that the teacher was read to; it also cannot take the direct object 'instructions' in this structure.

• Option 2 "reading the" leaves the sentence without a finite verb.

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "had reading" is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Tense formulas: had + V3 = past perfect; had been + V-ing = past perfect continuous; was/were + V3 = simple past passive.

• The past perfect is used for the earlier of two past actions: The teacher had read the instructions before the exam began.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Peoples might confess just to get out of the interrogation room.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Peoples might confess

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the word "Peoples". In the sense of persons / human beings, "people" is already plural and never takes an -s.

◦ Correct usage: Many people were waiting outside. (not 'peoples')

◦ The form "peoples" is used only in the different sense of nations, races or communities: the peoples of Asia, indigenous peoples.

◦ Corrected sentence: People might confess just to get out of the interrogation room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment "just to get out of" is correct — the infinitive of purpose with the phrasal verb get out of (to escape from).

• Segment "the interrogation room." is correct — the definite article is properly used with the specific room.

• The modal "might" correctly expresses possibility.

NOTE

• Nouns that are always plural in form: scissors, trousers, spectacles, tongs, cattle, police, poultry.

• Nouns that look plural but are singular: news, mathematics, physics, politics, economics, measles.

• Other uncountables that take no -s: information, furniture, luggage, advice, equipment, machinery, scenery.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The new government's domestic policies could easily undermine the main foreign policy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Enhance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Undermine" means to weaken or damage something gradually, especially somebody's authority, confidence or position. (कमज़ोर करना)

◦ Its antonym must mean to strengthen or improve, and "Enhance" means to increase or improve the quality, value or extent of something. (बढ़ाना)

◦ Example: Constant criticism undermined her confidence, while genuine praise would have enhanced it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Cripple" = to damage seriously or make unable to function — a synonym of undermine, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Weaken" = to make less strong — the closest synonym of undermine, deliberately placed as a trap.

• Option 3 "Spoil" = to damage or ruin — again similar in sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of undermine: weaken, sabotage, subvert, erode, impair, sap.

• Antonyms of undermine: enhance, strengthen, reinforce, bolster, buttress, fortify.

• Literally, to undermine is to dig beneath something (a mine under a wall) so that it collapses — a useful image for remembering the meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I was really hoping to ______ a decent movie this time, and I came up with an undisputed classic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. unearth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unearth" means to find or discover something after searching for it (literally, to dig out of the ground). (खोज निकालना)

◦ The sentence is about searching for and finding a good film, and the second half — "I came up with an undisputed classic" — confirms the idea of discovery.

◦ Correct: I was really hoping to unearth a decent movie this time, and I came up with an undisputed classic.

◦ Grammar point: after "hoping to", the base form of the verb is required, and 'unearth' is a verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tirade" is a noun meaning a long angry speech of criticism, so it cannot follow 'to' as a verb.

• Option 2 "subside" = to become less intense or to sink to a lower level; it is intransitive and cannot take 'a movie' as its object.

• Option 4 "strut" = to walk in a proud, self-important way.

NOTE

• Synonyms of unearth: discover, uncover, dig up, expose, ferret out, bring to light.

• "Come up with" means to find or produce an answer, idea or solution; "undisputed" means accepted by everyone, beyond question.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Glovve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is wrongly spelt; the correct spelling is "Glove" — g-l-o-v-e, with a single 'v' and a silent final e.

◦ A glove is a covering for the hand with separate parts for each finger. (दस्ताना)

◦ English words very rarely double the letter v — hence glove, love, above, move, prove all take a single v.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Wider" is correct — the comparative of wide (wide – wider – widest).

• Option 3 "Hide" is correct — to conceal (hide – hid – hidden); as a noun it also means an animal's skin.

• Option 4 "Fold" is correct — to bend something over on itself; also an enclosure for sheep.

NOTE

• Useful idioms with glove: hand in glove (with) = in very close association, usually for a dishonest purpose; fit like a glove = to fit perfectly; handle with kid gloves = to treat very gently.

• Similar single/double-letter traps: coming (not comming), writing (not writting), traveller/traveler, beginning (double n).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

The black sheep
option_4: The least reputable member of a group
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The least reputable member of a group.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "black sheep (of the family)" refers to a person who is regarded as a disgrace or an embarrassment to a family or group — its least respectable member. (कुलकलंक)

◦ Example: He gambled away the family fortune and was always called the black sheep of the family.

◦ Origin: in a flock of white sheep, a black lamb stood out and its wool could not be dyed, so it was considered less valuable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A day of importance" corresponds to the idiom a red-letter day.

• Option 2 "A stupid or foolish person" is conveyed by expressions such as a blockhead or not the sharpest tool in the box.

• Option 3 "A friend who betrays" is a snake in the grass or a Judas.

NOTE

• Other colour idioms frequently asked in SSC: red-handed (in the act of doing wrong), red tape (excessive bureaucracy), green with envy, white elephant (a costly but useless possession), blue blood (aristocratic descent), once in a blue moon (very rarely), golden handshake (a large payment on leaving a job).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The comedian's jokes are so bad that audiences usually groaning instead of laugh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. usually groan instead of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed in the underlined part, and only Option 1 makes both correctly.

◦ The clause "that audiences ______ laugh" needs a finite verb, so the participle "groaning" must become the simple present "groan" (the plural subject audiences takes the base form).

◦ "Usually" is the correct adverb of frequency modifying the verb groan; the adjective 'usual' cannot modify a verb.

◦ "Instead of" is followed by the -ing form or a noun, and here "laugh" completes the comparison naturally in the printed sentence.

◦ Corrected sentence: The comedian's jokes are so bad that audiences usually groan instead of laughing/laugh.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "usual groan instead off" has two errors — the adjective 'usual' for the adverb, and off (away from) for of.

• Option 3 "usual groaned despite of" is wrong: "despite" is never followed by 'of' (correct forms: despite + noun, or in spite of + noun).

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong because the printed clause has no finite verb.

NOTE

• Position of adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never): before the main verb but after 'be' — She usually comes late; She is usually late.

• Remember: despite = in spite of (never 'despite of').

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. prefunctory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is wrongly spelt; the correct spelling is "perfunctory" — p-e-r-f-u-n-c-t-o-r-y, beginning with the prefix per-, not pre-.

◦ Perfunctory means done merely as a duty, without real interest, care or enthusiasm; superficial and hasty. (लापरवाही से किया गया)

◦ Example: He gave the report a perfunctory glance and signed it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "pernicious" is correct; it means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

• Option 3 "pariah" is correct; it means an outcast — a person rejected by society.

• Option 4 "peripheral" is correct; it means relating to the outer edge; of secondary importance.

NOTE

• Distinguish the prefixes per- (through, thoroughly — perform, persist, perfunctory) and pre- (before — prefix, predict, prepare).

• Synonyms of perfunctory: cursory, superficial, casual, mechanical, offhand. Antonyms: thorough, careful, diligent, painstaking.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

The pudding fell ______ floor with a heart-stopping crash.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "fall" takes the preposition "to" when we describe something dropping down onto the floor or the ground.

◦ Standard expressions: fall to the floor, fall to the ground, fall to pieces.

◦ Correct: The pudding fell to the floor with a heart-stopping crash.

◦ "To" here indicates the destination or end point of the downward movement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "upon the" is possible in formal or literary style but is not the natural collocation with fall + floor in ordinary usage.

• Option 2 "up to the" indicates movement upward or as far as, which contradicts falling.

• Option 3 "in to the" is wrongly split; even the correct form "into" would mean entering the inside of something, not landing on a surface.

NOTE

• Note the difference: in to (two words — the adverb in plus to: He came in to meet me) and into (one word, showing movement inside: He walked into the room).

• Other useful 'fall' collocations: fall ill, fall asleep, fall in love, fall behind, fall through (to fail).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Apple's success attracted the ______ of the computer giant IBM.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. attention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes after the definite article "the" and before the preposition "of", so the word required is a noun — and the noun of this family is "attention".

◦ "Attract the attention of" is a fixed collocation meaning to make somebody notice you.

◦ Correct: Apple's success attracted the attention of the computer giant IBM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "attending" is a participle/gerund; "the attending of" is not idiomatic here.

• Option 2 "attend" is a verb and cannot follow the article 'the'.

• Option 4 "attentive" is an adjective meaning paying close attention, and adjectives are not used in this noun slot.

NOTE

• Word family: attend (verb) – attention (noun) – attentive (adjective) – attentively (adverb) – attendance/attendant (nouns).

• Useful collocations with attention: pay attention to, draw attention to, attract attention, bring to somebody's attention, stand at attention.

• A structural clue worth remembering: article + ______ + of almost always requires a noun.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A place of refugee
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Asylum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Asylum" means a place of refuge and safety, especially protection given by a country to a person who has fled from another country. (शरण)

◦ Example: The dissident writer was granted political asylum.

◦ It also has the older sense of an institution for the care of the mentally ill (a lunatic asylum).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Home" is simply the place where one lives, without the sense of protection from danger.

• Option 3 "Shelter" means cover or protection from weather or danger; it is a general word, whereas the definition given points specifically to refuge for a refugee.

• Option 4 "Hospice" = a home providing care for the terminally ill.

NOTE

• Related vocabulary: refugee (a person forced to leave his country), asylum seeker, migrant, émigré, sanctuary (a place of safety, also a protected area for wildlife).

• Other one-word substitutions of place: orphanage (home for orphans), sanatorium (place for recovering patients), granary (store for grain), aviary (large cage for birds), arsenal (store for weapons).

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

I had a (toddler) at home and two other children at school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. newborn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "toddler" is a very young child who has just learnt to walk, usually between about one and three years old. (नन्हा बच्चा)

◦ Among the four options, only "newborn" refers to a very young child, so it is the closest in meaning; the sentence contrasts this small child at home with the two other children at school.

◦ The word comes from the verb "toddle" — to walk with short unsteady steps, as a small child does.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ancient" = belonging to the very distant past, used of times and objects, not of a child.

• Option 2 "adult" = a fully grown person — the opposite end of the age scale.

• Option 4 "senior" = older or higher in rank.

NOTE

• Stages of human age in English: infant/newborn → toddler → child → adolescent/teenager → adult → middle-aged → elderly.

• In such questions, choose the option that is closest in the given context, even if it is not an exact dictionary synonym — that is the standard SSC approach.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

In the logo, the blue contrast wells with its complementary colour, yellow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. contrasts well.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are required, and only Option 4 makes both.

◦ The subject is "the blue" — a singular noun (the colour blue) — so the verb must take -s: "contrasts".

◦ The word after the verb must be the adverb "well", describing how the colours contrast; "wells" (a verb meaning to flow up, or the plural noun wells) is wrong here.

◦ Corrected sentence: In the logo, the blue contrasts well with its complementary colour, yellow.

◦ Note the collocation "contrast with" = to show a clear difference when compared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because of the subject–verb agreement error.

• Option 2 "contrast well" corrects the adverb but leaves the plural verb with a singular subject.

• Option 3 "contrast we'll" is meaningless — "we'll" is the contraction of we will.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: a singular subject takes a verb with -s in the simple present (He plays), while a plural subject takes the base form (They play).

• Complementary = combining well to form a whole (complementary colours); complimentary = expressing praise, or given free of charge.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Draw a blank
option_4: To fail to get an answer or result
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To fail to get an answer or result.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "draw a blank" means to get no response or result; to fail to find what one is looking for, or to be unable to remember something. (कुछ हासिल न होना / याद न आना)

◦ Example: The police searched for weeks but drew a blank.

◦ Example: I tried to recall his name, but I drew a blank.

◦ Origin: it comes from lotteries, where a ticket drawn without a prize number on it was literally blank.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Give lame excuses" is expressed by idioms such as beat about the bush or simply make excuses.

• Option 2 "A very complex question" corresponds to a hard nut to crack.

• Option 3 "Ragging of a fresher" has no connection with this idiom.

NOTE

• Related 'failure' idioms: come to nothing, fall flat, bite the dust, go up in smoke, a wild goose chase (a hopeless search).

• Other 'draw' idioms: draw the line (to set a limit), draw a parallel (to point out a similarity), back to the drawing board (start again from the beginning).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Impossible
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Applicable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Impossible" means not able to be done, or not able to happen. (असंभव)

◦ Among the given options, "Applicable" — meaning relevant, suitable and able to be applied or put into practice — is the closest to the opposite idea, since something applicable can be carried out.

◦ The other three options all carry a sense of doubt or weakness, which is nearer to 'impossible' than opposite to it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Shaky" = unsteady, uncertain or weak.

• Option 3 "Unsure" = not confident or certain.

• Option 4 "Unlikely" = not probable — this is a matter of low probability, whereas 'impossible' means it cannot happen at all; it is therefore a near-synonym rather than an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of impossible: unattainable, unachievable, impracticable, unfeasible, hopeless.

• Antonyms of impossible: possible, feasible, practicable, attainable, achievable, applicable.

• Note the negative prefixes: im- before p, b, m (impossible, imbalance, immature); in- (incorrect); il- before l (illegal); ir- before r (irregular).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

These people remind me of a harmony that exists with the natural world. They know their environment in a (1) ______ that can only be acquired (2) ______ living on equal footing with the natural world, not in (3) ______ through a recognition that humans are dependent (4) ______ our surroundings, something those of us who live in towns and cities too (5) ______ forget.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. way.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows "They know their environment in a ______", and the standard English expression for describing the manner in which something is known or done is "in a way".

◦ The relative clause that follows — "that can only be acquired ..." — confirms this, because it is a way of knowing that is acquired through experience.

◦ Correct: They know their environment in a way that can only be acquired through living on equal footing with the natural world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "line" does not collocate with 'know ... in a'.

• Option 3 "time" would refer to a period, not a manner, and does not fit "acquired".

• Option 4 "style" refers to a manner of doing or presenting something, usually deliberate and personal; it does not suit knowledge gained by living close to nature.

NOTE

• Useful expressions with way: in a way (to some extent / in a manner), by the way (incidentally), in the way (blocking), give way (to yield), make way (to clear space).

• In cloze tests, read the clause that follows the blank — it usually fixes which noun is required.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

These people remind me of a harmony that exists with the natural world. They know their environment in a (1) ______ that can only be acquired (2) ______ living on equal footing with the natural world, not in (3) ______ through a recognition that humans are dependent (4) ______ our surroundings, something those of us who live in towns and cities too (5) ______ forget.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. through.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a preposition meaning "by means of", because the knowledge is acquired by the process of living close to nature — and that preposition is "through".

◦ "Through" is regularly used to show the means or method: success through hard work, learning through experience.

◦ It is also followed here by the -ing form "living", which is exactly what a preposition requires.

◦ Correct: ... a way that can only be acquired through living on equal footing with the natural world.

◦ The same word appears again later in the passage — "through a recognition that humans are dependent ..." — which confirms the writer's pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "for" indicates purpose or duration, not means.

• Option 3 "to" would need a different structure and cannot show method here.

• Option 4 "with" indicates accompaniment or instrument, which does not fit "acquired ______ living".

NOTE

• Prepositions are always followed by a noun or an -ing form, never by a base verb: good at swimming, after finishing work.

• "On equal footing with" means on an equal basis; in a position of equality.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

These people remind me of a harmony that exists with the natural world. They know their environment in a (1) ______ that can only be acquired (2) ______ living on equal footing with the natural world, not in (3) ______ through a recognition that humans are dependent (4) ______ our surroundings, something those of us who live in towns and cities too (5) ______ forget.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. domination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence sets up a contrast: knowledge acquired by living on equal footing with nature, "not in ______".

◦ The natural opposite of equal footing is domination — controlling or ruling over nature rather than living as its equal. (प्रभुत्व)

◦ Correct: ... acquired through living on equal footing with the natural world, not in domination ...

◦ The whole passage praises harmony with nature, so the rejected alternative is the attitude of mastery over it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "opposition" means resistance or disagreement; one does not "know the environment in opposition", and it is not the opposite of equal footing.

• Option 3 "corporation" = a large business organisation, or a municipal body.

• Option 4 "collection" = a group of things gathered together.

NOTE

• Word family: dominate (verb) – domination/dominance (nouns) – dominant/domineering (adjectives).

• The passage reflects the idea of environmental sustainability — living in balance with nature instead of exploiting it.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

These people remind me of a harmony that exists with the natural world. They know their environment in a (1) ______ that can only be acquired (2) ______ living on equal footing with the natural world, not in (3) ______ through a recognition that humans are dependent (4) ______ our surroundings, something those of us who live in towns and cities too (5) ______ forget.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "dependent" is always followed by the preposition "on" (or upon).

◦ Correct: ... a recognition that humans are dependent on our surroundings.

◦ Example: Children are dependent on their parents; the crop is dependent on the monsoon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "to", Option 3 "in" and Option 4 "of" are all wrong, because "dependent" does not collocate with any of them.

• Note the related spellings: dependent (adjective — He is dependent on her) and dependant (noun in British English — He has three dependants).

NOTE

• Other adjective + preposition pairs frequently tested by SSC: afraid of, aware of, capable of, fond of, jealous of; good at, bad at, expert at/in; interested in, rich in; similar to, superior to, inferior to, prone to; angry with (a person), angry at (a thing); satisfied with, popular with.

• Verb form: depend on — It depends on the weather (never 'depends of').

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

These people remind me of a harmony that exists with the natural world. They know their environment in a (1) ______ that can only be acquired (2) ______ living on equal footing with the natural world, not in (3) ______ through a recognition that humans are dependent (4) ______ our surroundings, something those of us who live in towns and cities too (5) ______ forget.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. easily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression required is "too easily forget", meaning forget far too readily, without difficulty or thought.

◦ The writer's point is that city dwellers lose sight of their dependence on nature all too readily, and "too easily" carries exactly this note of mild reproach.

◦ Correct: ... something those of us who live in towns and cities too easily forget.

◦ Grammar point: "too + adverb + verb" is a standard structure — too quickly judge, too easily forget.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "highly" modifies adjectives and participles (highly successful, highly regarded), not the verb 'forget' in this way.

• Option 2 "marginally" = slightly, to a small extent, which weakens rather than strengthens the writer's criticism.

• Option 4 "equally" = to the same degree, and there is no comparison being drawn here.

NOTE

• The phrase "all too easily" is a common English collocation expressing regret that something happens far too readily.

• Adverbs are formed from adjectives by adding -ly: easy → easily (y changes to i), happy → happily, quick → quickly.

question: GDP calculated at some constant set of prices is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is real GDP.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Real GDP is the Gross Domestic Product calculated at a constant set of prices, that is, at the prices of a chosen base year. It is therefore also called GDP at constant prices.

◦ Because prices are held constant, real GDP removes the effect of inflation and shows the true change in the volume of output.

• Nominal GDP is GDP calculated at the current year's prices (GDP at current prices); it rises both when output rises and when prices rise.

• The relationship between the two is given by the GDP Deflator:

◦ GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100

◦ It is a broad measure of the general price level in the economy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the money value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a year.

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad; NNP = GNP – Depreciation; NNP at factor cost = National Income.

• Per capita income = National Income ÷ Total Population.

NOTE

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• The first attempt to estimate India's national income was made by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"; after independence, the National Income Committee (1949) was set up under the chairmanship of P. C. Mahalanobis.

question: Who was the last Governor General of British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Mountbatten.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Louis Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and Governor-General of British India; he took charge in March 1947 and oversaw the Partition and transfer of power on 15 August 1947.

◦ The Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) provided for the partition of India, and it was implemented through the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

◦ After independence he continued as the first Governor-General of the Dominion of India (1947–48).

• C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General of independent India (1948–1950) and the only Indian to hold the post.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lord Wellesley (1798–1805) introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system.

• Lord Hastings (1813–23) fought the Anglo-Nepal War and the Third Anglo-Maratha War, and introduced the Ryotwari system in Madras.

• Lord Auckland (1836–42) is remembered for the disastrous First Anglo-Afghan War.

NOTE

• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773); Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (1833); Lord Canning was the first Viceroy of India (1858).

• The Government of India Act, 1858 created the post of Viceroy, and the Charter Act of 1833 created the post of Governor-General of India.

question: Which of the following crop is also known as "Golden fibre"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jute is known as the "Golden Fibre" because of its shining golden-brown colour and its high commercial value.

• Conditions of growth: it needs high temperature (25–35°C), heavy rainfall (150–250 cm) and well-drained alluvial soil renewed every year by floods.

◦ It is grown mainly in West Bengal, Bihar, Assam, Odisha and Meghalaya, with West Bengal the leading producer.

◦ It is used for making gunny bags, mats, ropes, yarn, carpets and other artefacts, and is valued today as a biodegradable, eco-friendly fibre.

• India is the largest producer of jute, while Bangladesh is the largest exporter of jute goods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other nicknames of crops: Cotton – "White Gold"; Tea – the beverage crop of the hills; Coffee – "black gold"; Coconut – "Kalpavriksha".

• Rice is a kharif crop requiring high temperature and above 100 cm rainfall; Wheat is the main rabi crop of northern India; Sugarcane is a long-duration tropical crop, with Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra the leading producers.

NOTE

• Cropping seasons in India: Kharif (sown June–July, harvested September–October — rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton), Rabi (sown October–December, harvested April–June — wheat, barley, gram, mustard) and Zaid (summer season — watermelon, cucumber, fodder).

• The first jute mill in India was set up at Rishra, near Kolkata, in 1855.

question: Jama Masjid in Delhi was built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jama Masjid of Delhi (originally Masjid-i-Jahan Numa) was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656.

◦ It is one of the largest mosques in India, built of red sandstone and white marble, and stands opposite the Red Fort in Old Delhi.

• Shah Jahan (1628–1658) is called the "Prince among Builders" or the "Engineer King", and his reign is regarded as the Golden Age of Mughal architecture.

◦ His other constructions: the Taj Mahal (Agra, for Mumtaz Mahal), the Red Fort and Shahjahanabad (Delhi), the Moti Masjid (Agra Fort) and the famous Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Alauddin Khilji built the Alai Darwaza (1311) and Siri Fort, and introduced market/price control reforms.

• Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri, including the Buland Darwaza (to commemorate his Gujarat victory) and the Ibadat Khana.

• Sikandar Lodi founded the city of Agra in 1504 and shifted his capital there.

NOTE

• The Taj Mahal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983; the Red Fort Complex was inscribed in 2007 and Qutub Minar in 1993.

• Qutub Minar was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

question: In June 2022, Google Doodle honoured Satyendra Nath Bose, he was an/a ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Physicist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) was a distinguished Indian physicist and mathematician, honoured by a Google Doodle in June 2022.

• His major contribution:

◦ In 1924 he sent his paper on the statistics of light quanta to Albert Einstein, and their joint work produced the Bose-Einstein statistics and the theory of the Bose-Einstein condensate.

◦ The class of particles that obey these statistics — such as photons — was named "boson" after him by Paul Dirac.

◦ The much-discussed "God Particle", the Higgs boson, carries his name in its second half.

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and was made a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1958.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other great Indian scientists: C. V. Raman (Nobel Prize in Physics, 1930, for the Raman Effect), Homi J. Bhabha (father of India's nuclear programme), Vikram Sarabhai (father of India's space programme), Srinivasa Ramanujan (mathematician) and Jagadish Chandra Bose (plant physiology and radio research).

• National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February, the day the Raman Effect was discovered.

NOTE

• Particles are of two classes: bosons (integer spin, obeying Bose-Einstein statistics) and fermions (half-integer spin, obeying Fermi-Dirac statistics and the Pauli exclusion principle).

• The S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences in Kolkata is named after him.

question: Which of the following article of Indian constitution is related with "Separation of Judiciary from Executive"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 50.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 50 of the Constitution directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.

• It is one of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution, borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland.

◦ DPSPs are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by any court — but they are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

• Other important DPSPs:

◦ Article 40 – Organisation of Village Panchayats.

◦ Article 44 – Uniform Civil Code for all citizens.

◦ Article 46 – Promotion of the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and other weaker sections.

◦ Article 47 – Duty to raise the level of nutrition and to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs.

◦ Article 48 – Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry; prohibition of the slaughter of cows and other milch cattle.

◦ Article 51 – Promotion of international peace and security.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers in management) and Article 48A (protection of environment and wildlife) were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

• Article 38(2), on minimising inequalities in income, was added by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

NOTE

• DPSPs are classified as Socialistic, Gandhian and Liberal-Intellectual in nature; Article 40 (Village Panchayats) is a Gandhian principle.

• In the Minerva Mills case (1980) the Supreme Court held that a balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs is part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

question: Lata Mangeshkar recorded her first playback song for a ________ film.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marathi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lata Mangeshkar recorded her first playback song, "Naachu Yaa Gade, Khelu Saari Mani Haus Bhaari", for the Marathi film "Kiti Hasaal" in 1942; she was then only about thirteen.

◦ She was born on 28 September 1929 at Indore and belonged to a Marathi-speaking family; her father Deenanath Mangeshkar was a classical singer and theatre artist.

◦ She sang in over thirty-six Indian languages in a career of more than seven decades and was known as the "Nightingale of India" and the "Queen of Melody".

• Major honours:

◦ Bharat Ratna (2001) — she was the second singer after M. S. Subbulakshmi to receive it.

◦ Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989), Padma Bhushan (1969) and Padma Vibhushan (1999).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Her famous song "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon", written by Kavi Pradeep and composed by C. Ramchandra, was first sung in 1963 before Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

• Her younger sister Asha Bhosle received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2000.

NOTE

• Lata Mangeshkar passed away on 6 February 2022.

• The Government of India observes 28 September as a day marking her birth anniversary; the Lata Mangeshkar Award is instituted by the governments of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

question: Jhijhiya is a famous folk dance of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jhijhiya is a famous folk dance of the Mithila region of Bihar (also performed in parts of Jharkhand and the neighbouring Terai region).

◦ It is performed mainly by women during Dussehra/Navratri, in worship of Goddess Durga.

◦ The dancers balance earthen pots with many holes and a lighted lamp inside on their heads while dancing and singing.

◦ Traditionally it is associated with prayers for the welfare of the family and for protection from black magic.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Bihar: Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Paika, Jhumeri, Sama Chakeva and Kajari.

• Madhubani (Mithila) painting is the famous folk art of the same region and has a GI tag.

• Folk dances of other states: Ghoomar, Kalbelia (Rajasthan), Ras Leela, Charkula (Uttar Pradesh), Ghoomar/Saang (Haryana).

NOTE

• Important folk dances to remember: Bihu (Assam), Garba/Dandiya Raas (Gujarat), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Lavani/Tamasha (Maharashtra), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/West Bengal), Yakshagana (Karnataka), Theyyam/Kaikottikali (Kerala) and Rouf (Jammu & Kashmir).

• The capital of Bihar is Patna, and Bihar Diwas is celebrated on 22 March.

question: "Thomas Cup" is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Thomas Cup is the world men's team championship in Badminton, organised by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).

◦ It was started in 1948-49 and is named after Sir George Alan Thomas, a former English badminton player and administrator.

◦ India won the Thomas Cup for the first time in 2022, defeating Indonesia 3-0 in the final at Bangkok, Thailand — a historic first in 73 years.

• The Uber Cup is the corresponding women's team championship in badminton, named after Betty Uber.

• The Sudirman Cup is the mixed team world championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Trophies and their sports: Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Irani Cup, Deodhar Trophy – Cricket; Santosh Trophy, Durand Cup, Subroto Cup – Football; Davis Cup (men) and Billie Jean King Cup (women) – Tennis; Agha Khan Cup, Beighton Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy – Hockey.

• Famous Indian badminton players: Prakash Padukone (first Indian to win the All England Championship, 1980), Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal, P. V. Sindhu (Olympic silver 2016, bronze 2020) and Lakshya Sen.

NOTE

• Badminton terms: smash, drop shot, deuce, let, service court, shuttlecock.

• The BWF headquarters is at Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; badminton became an Olympic sport in 1992 (Barcelona).

question: The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ignition temperature.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ignition temperature is the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire (starts burning).

◦ A substance will not burn below this temperature, however much fuel or oxygen is present.

◦ Substances with a very low ignition temperature, such as petrol, alcohol and phosphorus, are called inflammable (flammable) substances.

• The three essential requirements for combustion are:

◦ Fuel, Air (oxygen) and Heat to raise the fuel to its ignition temperature.

◦ Fire is extinguished by removing any one of these three — for example, water cools the fuel below its ignition temperature, and a CO₂ extinguisher cuts off the oxygen supply.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid; the boiling point is where a liquid changes into a gas.

• Types of combustion: rapid combustion (LPG burning), spontaneous combustion (phosphorus catching fire on its own), and explosion (sudden combustion producing heat, light, sound and a large volume of gas).

NOTE

• Carbon dioxide is the best extinguisher for electrical and oil fires, because water conducts electricity and oil floats on water.

• The calorific value of a fuel is the amount of heat produced by burning 1 kg of it completely, measured in kilojoules per kg (kJ/kg); hydrogen has the highest calorific value.

question: The reproduction process in which only a single parent is involved is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is asexual reproduction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Asexual reproduction is the process in which only a single parent is involved, and no fusion of gametes (fertilisation) takes place.

◦ The offspring produced are genetically identical to the parent and are called clones.

• Main methods of asexual reproduction:

◦ Binary fission — Amoeba, Bacteria, Paramecium.

◦ Multiple fission — Plasmodium.

◦ Budding — Hydra, Yeast.

◦ Fragmentation — Spirogyra.

◦ Regeneration — Planaria.

◦ Spore formation — Rhizopus (bread mould), ferns.

◦ Vegetative propagation — potato (tubers/eyes), onion (bulb), ginger (rhizome), rose and sugarcane (stem cuttings), Bryophyllum (leaf buds).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of male and female gametes, producing offspring with genetic variation — the raw material of evolution.

• External fertilisation takes place outside the body (frogs, fish), while internal fertilisation occurs inside the female body (humans, birds, reptiles).

• In vitro fertilisation (IVF) is fertilisation carried out in the laboratory, outside the body; the resulting baby is popularly called a "test-tube baby".

NOTE

• Dolly the sheep (1996) was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell.

• India's first test-tube baby, Harsha Chawda (Kanupriya Agarwal), was born in 1978 through the work of Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay.

question: 'The Inheritance of Loss' book is written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kiran Desai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Inheritance of Loss" (2006) was written by the Indian-born author Kiran Desai.

◦ It won the Man Booker Prize in 2006 and the National Book Critics Circle Award.

◦ The novel is set in Kalimpong, in the Himalayan foothills, against the background of the Gorkhaland agitation, and also follows an Indian immigrant in New York.

◦ Her first novel was "Hullabaloo in the Guava Orchard" (1998).

• She is the daughter of the celebrated novelist Anita Desai, who was shortlisted for the Booker Prize three times.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• V. S. Naipaul won the Booker Prize (1971) for In a Free State and the Nobel Prize in Literature (2001); he wrote the India trilogy — An Area of Darkness, India: A Wounded Civilization and India: A Million Mutinies Now.

• Ruskin Bond wrote The Room on the Roof, The Blue Umbrella and Rusty series; he received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1992) and the Padma Bhushan (2014).

• Salman Rushdie won the Booker Prize (1981) for Midnight's Children, which was later awarded the Booker of Bookers.

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006) and Aravind Adiga (2008).

• Geetanjali Shree won the International Booker Prize 2022 for "Tomb of Sand" (Ret Samadhi).

question: Which of the following is the ultimate source of energy for all living organisms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sun is the ultimate source of energy for all living organisms on the earth.

◦ Green plants (producers/autotrophs) capture solar energy and convert it into chemical energy in the form of food through photosynthesis:

◦ 6CO₂ + 6H₂O --(sunlight, chlorophyll)--> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

◦ This energy then flows through the food chain from producers to herbivores (primary consumers), then to carnivores, and finally to decomposers.

• Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional, and according to Lindeman's 10 per cent law, only about 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Energy in the Sun is produced by nuclear fusion, in which hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium.

• Even fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) store solar energy trapped by plants and animals millions of years ago; wind and hydel energy are also indirectly derived from solar energy.

• Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach the earth.

NOTE

• Chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, absorbs mainly the blue and red parts of sunlight and reflects green.

• The International Solar Alliance (ISA), headquartered at Gurugram, India, was launched jointly by India and France in 2015 at the Paris Climate Conference.

question: Which bill led to people staging a widespread protest in Delhi, Haryana, and Punjab in September 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Farmers Bill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The three farm bills passed by Parliament in September 2020 led to widespread and prolonged protests by farmers, especially from Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, at the borders of Delhi.

• The three laws were:

◦ The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020.

◦ The Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020.

◦ The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020.

• The farmers' main demands concerned the continuation of the Minimum Support Price (MSP) and the mandi (APMC) system.

• The three laws were repealed by the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021, passed in November–December 2021.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Agriculture is a subject of the State List, while trade and commerce fall in the Concurrent List — a point central to the debate on these laws.

• The MSP is announced by the government on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), set up in 1965.

NOTE

• A Bill becomes an Act after passage by both Houses and the assent of the President under Article 111.

• Related farm schemes: PM-KISAN (₹6,000 per year to farmer families), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (crop insurance) and e-NAM (National Agriculture Market, launched 2016).

question: The Ahmadiyya forms a sect of Islam which originated from India. It was founded by ______ in 1889.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ahmadiyya movement was founded in 1889 by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad at Qadian, in the Punjab (present-day Gurdaspur district).

◦ It is therefore also called the Qadiani movement.

◦ The movement was influenced by Western liberal thought and stressed universal religion, humanity and peaceful propagation, opposing jihad by the sword.

◦ It supported the spread of modern Western education among Indian Muslims.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in Bengal (1818), which later, under his son Dudu Miyan, took a strong anti-zamindar and anti-British turn.

• Mir Nisar Ali, popularly known as Titu Mir, led a peasant uprising in Bengal against zamindars and the British, and built the famous bamboo fort at Narkelberia.

• Shah Waliullah (1703–1762) of Delhi was an important Islamic reformer who translated the Quran into Persian and sought to reconcile the different Muslim schools of thought.

NOTE

• Other Muslim reform movements: the Aligarh Movement of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (who founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College, 1875, which became AMU in 1920), the Deoband Movement (1866) and the Wahabi Movement of Syed Ahmad Barelvi.

• Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote "Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind" (The Causes of the Indian Revolt).

question: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma was honoured with Kalidasa Samman in 1997-1998. She was famous for which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma (1915–1999) was the celebrated dancer and guru known as the "mother of Mohiniyattam" for her work in reviving and systematising the dance form.

◦ She was honoured with the Kalidasa Samman for 1997-1998.

◦ She wrote the important book "Mohiniyattam: History and Dance Structure".

• Mohiniyattam is the classical dance of Kerala:

◦ The name comes from "Mohini", the enchantress form of Lord Vishnu, and attam (dance).

◦ It is a solo dance performed by women, marked by gentle, swaying, lasya movements, with dancers wearing white or off-white kasavu sarees with a gold border.

◦ It was patronised and revived by the Travancore king Swathi Thirunal, and later by the poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, who founded the Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other exponents of Mohiniyattam: Sunanda Nair, Kanak Rele, Bharati Shivaji and Jayaprabha Menon.

• Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh) was developed by Siddhendra Yogi; Odissi (Odisha) is associated with Kelucharan Mohapatra; Kathak (Uttar Pradesh) has the Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas.

NOTE

• The Kalidasa Samman is awarded by the Government of Madhya Pradesh (instituted 1980) in classical music, classical dance, theatre and plastic arts.

• Kerala's classical dances: Kathakali (dance-drama, male dominated) and Mohiniyattam (solo, female); Koodiyattam is its Sanskrit theatre form recognised by UNESCO.

question: Who among the following Gupta rulers launched the Nalanda University?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumaragupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by the Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I (415–455 CE) in the 5th century CE, in present-day Nalanda district of Bihar.

◦ It grew into the most renowned Buddhist monastic university in the ancient world, attracting students from China, Korea, Tibet and South-East Asia.

◦ The Chinese pilgrims Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) and I-tsing studied here; Hiuen Tsang came to India during the reign of Harshavardhana.

◦ It was destroyed around 1193 CE by Bakhtiyar Khalji, and its ruins were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

◦ Kumaragupta I also issued coins bearing the title Mahendraditya.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) defeated the Shakas and took the title Shakari; the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign, and the Navaratnas including Kalidasa are traditionally associated with his court.

• Skandagupta successfully repelled the Huna invasions and repaired the Sudarshana Lake in Saurashtra.

• The Gupta dynasty was founded by Sri Gupta; Chandragupta I was the first great ruler, and Samudragupta is called the "Napoleon of India" (a title given by the historian V. A. Smith), whose achievements are recorded in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) composed by Harisena.

NOTE

• The Gupta age (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" for its achievements in literature, art, science and mathematics — Aryabhata, Varahamihira and Brahmagupta belonged to this era.

• The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli, Delhi, famous for its rust resistance, belongs to the Gupta period.

question: How many silver medals were won by India in London Olympics 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Two.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the London Olympics 2012, India won a total of 6 medals — 2 silver and 4 bronze — which was, at that time, India's best-ever performance at a single Olympic Games.

• The two silver medals were won by:

◦ Vijay Kumar — Shooting (25 m rapid fire pistol).

◦ Sushil Kumar — Wrestling (66 kg freestyle); he thus became the first Indian to win individual medals at two consecutive Olympics (bronze in Beijing 2008 and silver in London 2012).

• The four bronze medals were won by:

◦ Gagan Narang — Shooting (10 m air rifle).

◦ Saina Nehwal — Badminton (women's singles) — India's first Olympic medal in badminton.

◦ Mary Kom — Boxing (flyweight, 51 kg).

◦ Yogeshwar Dutt — Wrestling (60 kg freestyle).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 India won 7 medals (1 gold, 2 silver, 4 bronze) — its best tally so far — with Neeraj Chopra winning gold in the javelin throw.

• Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold in shooting at Beijing 2008.

NOTE

• The modern Olympic Games began at Athens in 1896, revived by Baron Pierre de Coubertin; the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland.

• The Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together), the word Communiter having been added in 2021.

question: Who was the first ruler of the Sayyid Dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khizr Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sayyid dynasty was founded by Khizr Khan in 1414, and it ruled the Delhi Sultanate until 1451.

◦ Khizr Khan had been appointed governor of Multan by Timur after his invasion of India in 1398, and he captured Delhi after the fall of the Tughlaqs.

◦ He never assumed the title of Sultan, ruling instead as Rayat-i-Ala (a viceroy) and continuing to acknowledge the suzerainty of Timur's successors.

• Rulers of the Sayyid dynasty in order: Khizr Khan (1414–21) → Mubarak Shah (1421–34) → Muhammad Shah (1434–45) → Alauddin Alam Shah (1445–51).

◦ Alauddin Alam Shah, the last ruler, abdicated in favour of Bahlol Lodi, who founded the Lodi dynasty in 1451.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526): Slave/Mamluk (1206–90), Khilji (1290–1320), Tughlaq (1320–1414), Sayyid (1414–51) and Lodi (1451–1526).

• Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi, written by Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi, is the chief source for the history of the Sayyid dynasty.

NOTE

• The Delhi Sultanate ended with the defeat of Ibrahim Lodi by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

• Razia Sultan (of the Slave dynasty) was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

question: The Mughals were descendants of ______ from their father's side.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Timur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mughals were descendants of Timur (Tamerlane) from their father's side, and of Genghis Khan from their mother's side.

◦ Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, was a fifth-generation descendant of Timur through his father Umar Shaikh Mirza, the ruler of Farghana.

◦ Through his mother he was a fourteenth-generation descendant of Genghis Khan.

◦ The Mughals themselves preferred to be called Timurids rather than Mughals, since the word Mughal (from Mongol) carried unpleasant associations of Genghis Khan's massacres.

• Timur invaded India in 1398 during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq and sacked Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur wrote his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), in Turkish; he won the First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi using field artillery and the Tulughma (flanking) tactic.

• He also won the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga, the Battle of Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans.

• Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192); Mahmud of Ghazni raided India seventeen times, including the sack of the Somnath temple (1025).

NOTE

• The Mughal Empire (1526–1857) reached its greatest territorial extent under Aurangzeb.

• Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl, and the Ain-i-Akbari is its third volume; Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri.

question: The streams of water flowing constantly on the ocean surface in definite directions are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ocean currents.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ocean currents are streams of water flowing constantly on the ocean surface in definite directions, rather like rivers within the sea.

◦ They are caused mainly by prevailing winds, differences in temperature and salinity (density), the rotation of the earth (Coriolis force) and the shape of the coastline.

• Ocean currents are of two types:

◦ Warm currents — flow from equatorial regions towards the poles (e.g., the Gulf Stream, the North Atlantic Drift, the Kuroshio and the Brazil Current).

◦ Cold currents — flow from polar regions towards the equator (e.g., the Labrador Current, the Humboldt (Peru) Current, the Benguela and the Canary Current).

• The meeting of warm and cold currents creates the world's richest fishing grounds — for example, the Grand Banks off Newfoundland, where the Gulf Stream meets the Labrador Current — but also causes dense fog.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Waves are the up-and-down oscillations of water caused mainly by winds; a tsunami is a giant wave caused by an undersea earthquake or volcanic eruption.

• Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea water caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun; spring tides occur on full moon and new moon days, and neap tides during the first and third quarters of the moon.

NOTE

• El Niño is the periodic warming of the surface waters of the eastern Pacific, which weakens the Indian monsoon; La Niña is its cold counterpart.

• The Gulf Stream keeps the ports of north-western Europe ice-free in winter.

question: The Yaoshang festival of Manipur is celebrated for ______ days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Yaoshang is the most important festival of Manipur, celebrated for five days beginning on the full moon day of Phalguna (February–March).

◦ It is the Manipuri equivalent of Holi, blending Vaishnava traditions with indigenous Meitei customs.

◦ Its highlight is the Thabal Chongba, a traditional moonlight folk dance in which boys and girls join hands and dance in a circle.

◦ Sports events and cultural competitions are held throughout the five days.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Manipur: Ningol Chakouba (a family festival for married daughters), Lai Haraoba, Kang (Rath Yatra), Cheiraoba (Manipuri New Year) and the Sangai Festival (the state tourism festival).

• Manipur's classical dance is Manipuri (Raas Leela); Thang-Ta is its famous martial art.

NOTE

• The capital of Manipur is Imphal; Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in North-East India, famous for its floating phumdis and the Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world, home to the Sangai deer.

• Manipur became a full-fledged State in 1972, along with Meghalaya and Tripura.

question: Thorny trees and bushes are found in which part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North – western.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Thorn forests and scrub (thorny trees and bushes) are found in the north-western part of India, in the semi-arid and arid regions.

◦ They occur in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and parts of Madhya Pradesh.

◦ These forests grow in areas receiving less than 70 cm of rainfall annually.

• Characteristics of thorn forests:

◦ Trees are scattered and have long roots that penetrate deep in search of water.

◦ Leaves are mostly thick, small or reduced to spines (thorns) to minimise the loss of water through transpiration — as in the cactus, whose stem is fleshy and stores water.

◦ Common species: acacia (babool), palms, euphorbias, khejri (the state tree of Rajasthan), khair, kikar and date palm.

◦ Common animals: camel, desert fox, wild ass, rats, mice and various reptiles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Types of natural vegetation in India: Tropical Evergreen Forests (over 200 cm rainfall — Western Ghats, north-east), Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon) Forests (the most widespread — teak, sal), Thorn Forests and Scrub, Montane Forests and Mangrove Forests (the Sundarbans, famous for the sundari tree and the Royal Bengal Tiger).

NOTE

• The India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published every two years by the Forest Survey of India (Dehradun).

• The National Forest Policy aims at bringing 33% of the geographical area under forest cover.

question: In November 2022, Indian Coast Guard Advanced Light Helicopter Mk-III squadron, 840 Sqn (CG), commissioned in ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Coast Guard's Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) Mk-III squadron, 840 Sqn (CG), was commissioned at Chennai, Tamil Nadu, in November 2022.

◦ The ALH Dhruv Mk-III is an indigenously designed and manufactured helicopter built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Bengaluru.

◦ It is fitted with advanced radar, electro-optic sensors, a medical intensive care unit and a heavy machine gun, making it suitable for search and rescue, maritime surveillance and medical evacuation.

◦ The squadron strengthens coastal security and search-and-rescue capability along the eastern seaboard, and it reflects the Aatmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) initiative in defence manufacturing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) was formally established on 1 February 1977 and given statutory status by the Coast Guard Act, 1978; it functions under the Ministry of Defence and is headquartered at New Delhi.

• Its motto is "Vayam Rakshamah" — We Protect.

• Its duties include protection of maritime interests, the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), marine environment protection and anti-smuggling operations.

NOTE

• India's EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline, and the territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles.

• Other indigenous defence platforms: INS Vikrant (India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, commissioned September 2022), the Tejas light combat aircraft and the Arjun main battle tank.

question: In countries like Japan, ______ birth rates make the population pyramid ______ at the base.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Low, Narrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In developed countries such as Japan, the birth rate is low, so fewer children are born each year and the number of people in the youngest age groups is small.

◦ Since the base of a population pyramid represents the youngest age group (0–4 years), a low birth rate makes the base narrow.

◦ Such a pyramid is also broader at the top, because low death rates and good healthcare mean a large elderly population — this shape is called a constrictive or declining pyramid.

• A population pyramid (age-sex pyramid) shows the distribution of a country's population by age group and sex.

◦ Males are usually shown on the left and females on the right.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• An expanding pyramid — with a broad base and narrow top — indicates high birth rates and high death rates, typical of developing countries such as Nigeria, Bangladesh and, to a lesser extent, India.

• A stationary pyramid — nearly bell-shaped — indicates birth and death rates that are both low and roughly equal, as in Australia.

• Japan faces an ageing population and a shrinking workforce, one of its major economic challenges.

NOTE

• Birth rate = number of live births per 1,000 people per year; Death rate = number of deaths per 1,000 people per year; Natural growth rate = birth rate – death rate.

• India is said to enjoy a "demographic dividend" because a large share of its population is in the working age group (15–59 years).
